display.purpose: Title-sheet wordmark only; expressed as authored SVG paths.

label.purpose: Compact, bold asset metadata such as release and issue labels.

components.name: Release Record
components.description: A full-width, square-corner dossier asset followed by factual Markdown and a direct repository link.
components.css: .ds-release { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:16px; border-top:2px solid #121212; border-bottom:1px solid #121212; padding:20px 0; color:#121212; font-family:Arial,sans-serif; } .ds-release-number { color:#F15A24; font:700 13px monospace; } .ds-release strong { flex:1; color:#173B82; font-size:24px; letter-spacing:-.04em; } .ds-release a { color:#173B82; font-weight:700; text-decoration-thickness:2px; text-underline-offset:3px; } .ds-release a:hover { color:#F15A24; } .ds-release a:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #F15A24; outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Dossier Title Sheet
components.description: A saturated cobalt masthead with paper rules, record labels, and an orange registration mark.
components.css: .ds-title { display:grid; gap:28px; background:#173B82; color:#F3F1E8; padding:36px; border:2px solid #F3F1E8; font-family:Arial,sans-serif; } .ds-title span, .ds-title small { font-size:11px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:.14em; } .ds-title strong { font-size:72px; font-weight:900; line-height:.8; letter-spacing:-.07em; }

narrative.overview: This is a public work record for an independent software maker. It treats each release as evidence: a named, numbered document with a concise factual description and a direct route to the repository. The visual language belongs to technical publishing rather than a generic developer portfolio—ink, paper, registration marks, rules, and diagrams do the identifying work.
keyCharacteristics: Saturated cobalt title sheets against warm off-white fields.
Safety orange used as a registration signal, not ambient decoration.
Full-width project dossiers with hard rules and one concise technical diagram each.
Direct repository links and factual copy in ordinary GitHub reading flow.

rules.name: The One-Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange is a measurement mark: reserve it for a small, high-information portion of an asset.

rules.name: The Flat Ink Rule
rules.body: Use flat fills and exact rules; gradients, glow, glass, and faux depth do not belong in this system.

rules.name: The Evidence-First Type Rule
rules.body: Display lettering establishes the record once; after that, the reader gets plain language, not ornamental type.

dos: Do make each asset explain a real release through a distinct, countable technical diagram.
Do retain ordinary Markdown descriptions and links below images so identity never replaces readable evidence.
Do keep the four-color ink-and-stock palette intact in authored profile assets.
Do use generous whitespace and hard rules to pace a scan through projects.
donts: Don't use dark-gradient heroes, neon glow, cyberpunk terminal theater, glass, or generic SaaS panel stacks.
Don't turn tools into a badge wall; describe the actual work first.
Don't add rounded cards, soft shadows, or pill-shaped controls to dossier assets.
Don't introduce commercial claims, testimonials, metrics, or product capabilities not evidenced by the linked repositories.
Don't retain exploratory mock pages after their composition decision has been implemented; the README and committed SVG assets are the sole source of visual truth.
